tools.description:
START HERE in any new conversation about a project. Returns a compact digest: what the project is, the active milestone, urgent and blocked work, recent decisions, every unresolved question, the glossary, what is deployed, and a suggested next action.

Call this before reading files or asking the human what is going on — it is one call and roughly 3–4k tokens. With no `project`, returns a one-line roll-up of every project plus anything at risk.

Pass `cwd` when you are in a repository. It scopes the digest to whichever project owns that checkout, and if none does it tells you so directly — rather than returning other projects and leaving you to conclude that yours is missing.

Open questions and glossary terms are never truncated. A missing open question makes you re-litigate something already settled; a missing glossary term makes you use the wrong word for a domain concept. Everything else degrades and the response reports what it dropped.

cwd.description: The absolute directory you are working in. Resolves to the project whose checkout contains it, and — when nothing matches — says so plainly instead of leaving you to infer it from a list of other projects. Always pass this when you are working in a repository.

depth.description: How much to include. `brief` is a few hundred tokens; `full` drops most limits.

project.description: Project id, slug or name. Omit for a cross-project roll-up.

session_id.description: A stable identifier for this conversation, minted once at first use and passed on every call. Specline never invents one: a stateless transport has no session to borrow, so provenance is cooperative. Omitting it still works, but the write is attributed only to 'some Claude session'.

since.description: Only summarise activity after this instant. Useful when resuming a conversation you already have context for.

tools.name: specline_context

tools.description:
Hybrid keyword and semantic search across every artifact that carries text, in every project. Use it to answer 'what do we know about X', 'has anyone raised this before', or 'what did customers say about onboarding'.

Searches specs, decisions, questions, feedback and design captions by meaning and by keyword together, and tasks, milestones, terms, environments, artifacts and projects by keyword. Metrics are deliberately excluded — they are numbers, and reaching them is a filter rather than a search.

Prefer a natural question over keywords; the semantic half is what makes 'why is billing slow' find a decision titled 'Aggregate hourly, not per-minute'.

Semantic search needs a daemon started with embeddings, and not every build carries one — so `searched` in the response names the halves that actually ran, and `not_searched` says why the others did not. When only the keyword half ran, no matches means no words matched; it is not evidence that the store holds nothing on the subject.

session_id.description: A stable identifier for this conversation, minted once at first use and passed on every call. Specline never invents one: a stateless transport has no session to borrow, so provenance is cooperative. Omitting it still works, but the write is attributed only to 'some Claude session'.

tools.name: specline_search

tools.description:
Fetch one or more artifacts by id, optionally with their prose body, their linked neighbours, or a diff between two revisions.

Use `depth` to pull in the graph around something — `specline_get(ids: [spec_id], depth: 2)` answers 'what implements this spec, and what do those things depend on' in one call. Use `version` to read an older revision and `diff_against` to see what changed between two.

depth.description: Also return linked neighbours to this depth. 0 means no traversal; 6 is the usual maximum worth asking for.

diff_against.description: Also return a unified diff between `version` (or the current revision) and this one.

direction.description: Which way to walk. Outbound follows edges away from the artifact ('what does this implement'); inbound follows edges into it ('what implements this').

ids.description: Prefixed ULIDs, e.g. tsk_01H8… The prefix says what the artifact is, so you never need to say.

include_body.description: Include the prose body for artifacts that have one.

rels.description: Restrict the traversal to these relations.

session_id.description: A stable identifier for this conversation, minted once at first use and passed on every call. Specline never invents one: a stateless transport has no session to borrow, so provenance is cooperative. Omitting it still works, but the write is attributed only to 'some Claude session'.

version.description: Read this document revision instead of the current one.

tools.name: specline_get

tools.description:
List projects, or resolve a name to one. **Call this before creating a project, every time.** It fuzzy-matches on name, slug, aliases and repository URL, and when anything plausible matches it returns `requires_confirmation: true` with the candidates.

When that happens, ask the human before creating anything. Nine near-duplicate projects is the failure mode that quietly ruins the cross-project view, and it is much cheaper to ask than to merge later.

query.description: A name, slug, alias or repo URL to match against. Omit to list everything.

session_id.description: A stable identifier for this conversation, minted once at first use and passed on every call. Specline never invents one: a stateless transport has no session to borrow, so provenance is cooperative. Omitting it still works, but the write is attributed only to 'some Claude session'.

tools.name: specline_projects

tools.description:
Every mutation since a timestamp or an event cursor, oldest first. Use it to catch up: 'what happened since I last looked', or to see what another session did while you were working.

Pass the `cursor` from a previous response to continue exactly where you left off, with no gaps and no repeats.

For one row's own story, read its notes with `specline_get` — a note says what was learned, where an event says only which field moved.

cursor.description: An event id from a previous response. Takes precedence over `since`.

session_id.description: A stable identifier for this conversation, minted once at first use and passed on every call. Specline never invents one: a stateless transport has no session to borrow, so provenance is cooperative. Omitting it still works, but the write is attributed only to 'some Claude session'.

tools.name: specline_activity

tools.description:
Create any of the thirteen artifact types. Returns the created artifact, so you never need to read it back.

Creates are idempotent: calling twice with the same project, type and title returns the existing artifact with `created: false` rather than making a duplicate. Whitespace and capitalisation are normalised, so 'Add login page' and 'add  Login  Page' are one task.

Before creating a **project**, call `specline_projects` first and confirm with the human (see that tool). Prefer consolidating into fewer, larger artifacts: a project with forty trivial tasks that should be eight is worse than useless.

body.description:
For prose-bearing types (spec, decision, question, feedback, design) this is written as the first document revision. For a task it is the short detail field — anything long-form belongs in a spec.

Write it the way you would say it to a colleague. Plain words, no padding, no sentence that exists to sound considered. Avoid "leverage", "utilize", "robust", "seamless", "delve", "in order to", "it's worth noting" — these are refused. Quoting an error message or what someone actually said is fine: put it in a code fence or a block quote and it is exempt.

definition.description: Glossary entries only: what the word means in this project. `body` is accepted for the same thing.

fields.description:
Any other column on the type: status, kind, priority, labels, target_date, severity, sentiment, url, and so on. Invalid values are rejected with the list of valid ones.

A `metric_observation` is recorded here too: `metric_id` (the `mtr_…` being measured), `value`, and an optional `observed_at`.

idempotency_key.description: Makes a retry a no-op instead of a duplicate. Derived from the project, type and normalised title when omitted, which is usually what you want — supply one only when two genuinely different things share a title.

image.description:
Design and artifact only: a small image, base64 encoded, or a `data:image/png;base64,…` URL.

**Keep this under about 100 KB.** You have to emit every base64 character, so 100 KB costs you roughly 35,000–45,000 output tokens and 1 MB costs 350,000 or more. The hard limit is 1 MB decoded and it is not a target. If the file is on the same machine, use `image_path` instead and none of this applies.

Put a Figma or web link in `body` when the image already lives somewhere.

image_path.description:
Design and artifact only: an absolute path to an image on the machine Specline is running on. The daemon reads the file itself, so the bytes never enter your context and a real screenshot costs you nothing.

This is the right way to attach anything bigger than a small mockup — up to 10 MB. Not a URL: the daemon makes no outbound requests on a model's instruction.

Readable folders only: Desktop, Downloads, Pictures, and the project's own directory. Anywhere else is refused and the refusal lists them. That is not about you — a path can be suggested by text you are reading rather than by the person you are talking to.

name.description: An alias for `title`, for the types whose column is called `name`.

project.description: Project id or slug. Required for everything except `project` itself, and optional for `term` — omitting it there defines the term globally.

session_id.description: A stable identifier for this conversation, minted once at first use and passed on every call. Specline never invents one: a stateless transport has no session to borrow, so provenance is cooperative. Omitting it still works, but the write is attributed only to 'some Claude session'.

slug.description: Projects only, and required for them: the URL-safe short name, unique across the store.

summary.description:
Tasks, milestones and feedback: REQUIRED. One or two plain sentences a colleague could read cold six weeks from now, without having been in this conversation. For a task: what is wrong or wanted, what it affects, and what done looks like. For a milestone: what the phase covers. For feedback this is the whole row — what somebody said, in their words, because feedback has no title to invent. It is what lists show, so a row without one means something only to whoever wrote it.

Write it like a person, not like a release note. No section references, no internal names, no rule-of-three lists, no sentence that exists to sound considered.

Good: "The board shows a task's priority but never which phase it belongs to, so you have to open each one to find out. Done when every row shows its milestone and you can group by it."

Bad: "Implement milestone surfacing on the board view per TQ-31 to improve organisational legibility."

term.description: An alias for `title`, for glossary entries.

title.description: The name. Called `name` on some types and `term` on glossary entries; `title` is accepted for all of them.

tools.name: specline_create

tools.description:
Change fields on an existing artifact, including status transitions. Returns the updated artifact.

**Not for prose.** A document body belongs to `specline_write_doc`, which versions it; this tool is for the fields around it — title, status, kind. Sending a body here would overwrite without a revision, and the previous author's text would be gone.

Pass the `version` you read. If someone else changed it since, the call is rejected with the current state and the events that happened in between, so you can usually merge and retry without asking anyone.

An accepted decision's content is immutable — supersede it with a new decision linked by `supersedes` rather than editing it. Use `archive: true` to soft-delete; nothing in Specline is ever really deleted.

To reorder a task, put `rank_after` or `rank_before` in `changes` naming another task — `{"rank_after": "KEEL-12"}` — rather than choosing a number. To make one task part of another, set `parent_id`; that is composition, and it is a different thing from `blocks`, which means "must happen first".

**Two task transitions belong to their own tools.** Starting work is `specline_claim`, which records who is on it; finishing is `specline_close`, which asks for the reason, the message and the evidence together. A `status` of `done` or `wont_do` sent here is refused without all three, so reaching for this tool to close something only costs you a round trip.

To attach an image to a design or artifact that already exists, put `image_path` in `changes` with an absolute path — the daemon reads the file, so the bytes never enter your context.

changes.description:
Fields to set. Unknown fields are rejected with the list of real ones.

Two are not fields but placements, for tasks: `rank_after` and `rank_before` each name another task and put this one next to it in the deliberate order. They resolve to `rank`, which you should not set directly.

One more is an instruction rather than a value: `image_path`, on a design or artifact, is an absolute path the daemon reads the image from. Do not set `blob_id` yourself.

idempotency_key.description: Makes a retry a no-op instead of a duplicate. Derived from the project, type and normalised title when omitted, which is usually what you want — supply one only when two genuinely different things share a title.

session_id.description: A stable identifier for this conversation, minted once at first use and passed on every call. Specline never invents one: a stateless transport has no session to borrow, so provenance is cooperative. Omitting it still works, but the write is attributed only to 'some Claude session'.

version.description: The `version` from when you read it. Not the document revision — that is `current_doc_version`.

tools.name: specline_update

tools.description:
Append a new revision of an artifact's prose body — for specs, decisions, questions, feedback and design captions.

Use this whenever the *content* of a document changes. Use `specline_update` instead for the fields around it: title, status, kind. The two are separate because a body is versioned and a status is not, and conflating them would either version every status flip or lose the history of every edit.

Always send the **full** body, not a patch — the revision is a snapshot. The previous one is kept and stays readable by version, and `specline_get` will diff any two. Writing content identical to the current revision is a no-op rather than a new version, so regenerating a document you have not changed is safe.

body.description:
The full markdown body.

Write it the way you would say it to a colleague. Plain words, no padding, no sentence that exists to sound considered. Avoid "leverage", "utilize", "robust", "seamless", "delve", "in order to", "it's worth noting" — these are refused. Quoting an error message or what someone actually said is fine: put it in a code fence or a block quote and it is exempt.

title.description: Update the title alongside the body. Omit to keep it.

tools.name: specline_write_doc

tools.description:
Append a note to any artifact — a finding, a gotcha, a measurement, a reason something was harder than expected. Use it the moment you learn something worth the next session knowing, not at the end.

This is the tool for the sentence that starts 'turns out…'. A task's status says a colour; its notes say what actually happened. Prefer a note over rewriting the artifact's body: notes accumulate and stay attributed to the conversation that wrote them, whereas a body is overwritten and the previous author's finding is gone.

Do not ask permission first — record it, then say in one line that you did. Notes are append-only: to withdraw one, pass `retract` with its id.

`body` is required unless you are passing `list` or `retract`.

body.description:
The note. One or two sentences beats a heading — say what you found and why it matters.

Write it the way you would say it to a colleague. Plain words, no padding, no sentence that exists to sound considered. Avoid "leverage", "utilize", "robust", "seamless", "delve", "in order to", "it's worth noting" — these are refused. Quoting an error message or what someone actually said is fine: put it in a code fence or a block quote and it is exempt.

id.description: The artifact to annotate. Any Specline id.

list.description: Return the artifact's existing notes instead of adding one.

retract.description: A note id (`nte_…`) to withdraw. Soft — it stays readable as a record of what was once believed.

session_id.description: A stable identifier for this conversation, minted once at first use and passed on every call. Specline never invents one: a stateless transport has no session to borrow, so provenance is cooperative. Omitting it still works, but the write is attributed only to 'some Claude session'.

tools.name: specline_note

tools.description:
Create or remove a typed edge. Direction matters and reads left to right: `from` does the verb to `to`.

A task **implements** a spec. A blocker **blocks** the thing waiting on it. A newer decision **supersedes** an older one. A decision **resolves** a question. Feedback **informs** a spec. If you find yourself wanting to say 'A depends on B', use `depends_on` and Specline will store it the right way round.

Use `anchor` to link to one requirement inside a spec (`REQ-4`) rather than the whole document — that is what makes traceability answerable per requirement.

anchor.description: A block inside the target, e.g. `REQ-4`. Omit for a whole-artifact link.

idempotency_key.description: Makes a retry a no-op instead of a duplicate. Derived from the project, type and normalised title when omitted, which is usually what you want — supply one only when two genuinely different things share a title.

remove.description: Archive the edge instead of creating it.

session_id.description: A stable identifier for this conversation, minted once at first use and passed on every call. Specline never invents one: a stateless transport has no session to borrow, so provenance is cooperative. Omitting it still works, but the write is attributed only to 'some Claude session'.

to.description: The artifact it is done to.

tools.name: specline_link

tools.description:
The answer to 'what should I do next', ranked. Open work with nothing live in its way, best first.

Call this rather than `specline_context` when the project is already familiar and the question is only what to pick up — the digest costs roughly 3,500 tokens and this costs a fraction of it.

The order is deliberate: **what a task unblocks comes before its priority**, so a p1 that releases three other tasks ranks above a p0 that releases nothing. Each row carries the reason it is where it is.

Parents are excluded, because their children are the actual work. Decisions waiting on a human are excluded too — they are in `specline_context`'s open questions, and nothing can start on them until someone answers.

Then `specline_claim` the one you pick, so the row says who is on it.

labels.description: Only tasks carrying **all** of these labels.

limit.description: How many to return. The response says how many were ready in total, so a cut list is never mistaken for the whole one.

milestone.description: Only work under this milestone — 'what is next in Phase 8' in one argument. An id or its name.

session_id.description: A stable identifier for this conversation, minted once at first use and passed on every call. Specline never invents one: a stateless transport has no session to borrow, so provenance is cooperative. Omitting it still works, but the write is attributed only to 'some Claude session'.

unclaimed.description: Only work nobody is holding. Pass this when another session may be running alongside you.

without_labels.description: Skip tasks carrying any of these labels.

tools.name: specline_next

tools.description:
Move a task to `in_progress` and record that this session is doing it. Call this **before** the work, not after — the point is that someone looking at the board can see what is happening now rather than only what has finished.

Refused if another session is already holding it, and the refusal names that session. A claim releases itself after three days, so a conversation that died mid-task does not hold work hostage, and `force` takes a live claim deliberately. Closing releases it immediately.

Re-claiming your own task is a no-op, so a retry costs nothing.

This needs your `session_id`. It is the one call that is refused without one: everywhere else an anonymous write is merely less traceable, but a claim naming nobody says the task is taken and not by whom.

force.description: Take a claim another session still holds. Use it when you know that session is gone.

idempotency_key.description: Makes a retry a no-op instead of a duplicate. Derived from the project, type and normalised title when omitted, which is usually what you want — supply one only when two genuinely different things share a title.

session_id.description: A stable identifier for this conversation, minted once at first use and passed on every call. Specline never invents one: a stateless transport has no session to borrow, so provenance is cooperative. Omitting it still works, but the write is attributed only to 'some Claude session'.

tools.name: specline_claim

tools.description:
Close a task with a reason, a message, and — for `done` — evidence. This is the tool for finishing work; `specline_update` can move a status but will refuse a terminal one without all of this, so use this instead of working around it.

The five reasons:
- `done` — finished. Needs a message and at least one piece of evidence.
- `wont_do` — deliberately not doing it. Needs a message.
- `duplicate` — the same work as another task. Names it, and draws a `duplicates` edge.
- `superseded` — replaced by another task. Names it, and draws a `supersedes` edge.
- `no_change` — looked at it, nothing needed doing. Needs a message.

Evidence is typed so that 'what shipped this week, with the commits' is a query rather than prose: `commit:<sha>`, `pr:<url>`, `test:<command>`, `doc:<entity-id>`, `url:<url>`, `image:<blob-id>`. A bare sha is refused.

The message is the one sentence that belongs to the transition. Anything else you learned along the way belongs in `specline_note`, which keeps accumulating.

**This also triages a signal.** Pass a `fbk_…` and the same three reasons mean what happens to a want rather than to work:
- `done` — picked up, or otherwise answered. Name what became of it as evidence; a `doc:spc_…` feature spec among it is linked to the signal. Not every want becomes a feature — some become a commit.
- `wont_do` — set down. The message is the argument, and it is appended to the signal so the same idea arriving in four months finds the reasoning instead of silence. Nothing is destroyed and it can be picked up again.
- `duplicate` — somebody had already asked. Names the other signal.

`superseded` and `no_change` are refused for a signal: neither describes what happens to a want. A signal cannot leave the Inbox without one of the three.

evidence.description: Typed proof, at least one for `done`: `commit:<sha>`, `pr:<url>`, `test:<command>`, `doc:<entity-id>`, `url:<url>`, `image:<blob-id>`.

idempotency_key.description: Makes a retry a no-op instead of a duplicate. Derived from the project, type and normalised title when omitted, which is usually what you want — supply one only when two genuinely different things share a title.

message.description:
What actually happened, in a sentence or two. What was built, or why it is not being done — it is what the next session reads instead of guessing from a status.

Write it the way you would say it to a colleague. Plain words, no padding, no sentence that exists to sound considered. Avoid "leverage", "utilize", "robust", "seamless", "delve", "in order to", "it's worth noting" — these are refused. Quoting an error message or what someone actually said is fine: put it in a code fence or a block quote and it is exempt.

other.description: For `duplicate` and `superseded` only: the task this one duplicates, or the one that replaced it.

session_id.description: A stable identifier for this conversation, minted once at first use and passed on every call. Specline never invents one: a stateless transport has no session to borrow, so provenance is cooperative. Omitting it still works, but the write is attributed only to 'some Claude session'.
